import HartshorneLib.Chapter4DifferentialDivisor
import HartshorneLib.Chapter4SmoothProperConsequences

/-!
# Degree of a canonical differential divisor

The divisor attached to a nonzero rational differential depends on the chosen
differential, while its degree does not.  Rescaling changes the divisor by a
principal divisor, and the smooth-proper product formula makes that principal
divisor have degree zero.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
variable (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral X.left]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom] [IsProper X.hom]

/-- Rescaling a nonzero rational differential leaves the degree of its divisor
unchanged.  The divisor itself changes by the principal divisor of the scalar.
The statement is choice-dependent in the differential, but its degree is
intrinsic to the resulting canonical divisor class. -/
theorem degree_differentialDivisor_smul_eq
    (a : X.left.functionFieldˣ)
    (ω : CurveRationalDifferentials X) (hω : ω ≠ 0)
    (haω : (a : X.left.functionField) • ω ≠ 0) :
    CurveDivisor.degree
        (differentialDivisor X ((a : X.left.functionField) • ω) haω) =
      CurveDivisor.degree (differentialDivisor X ω hω) := by
  rw [differentialDivisor_smul X a ω hω haω, CurveDivisor.degree_add]
  rw [principalDivisorsHaveDegreeZero_of_smoothProperIntegralCurve X a]
  simp

/-! The nonzero side condition for a unit rescaling is automatic. -/
theorem degree_differentialDivisor_smul_eq_of_nonzero
    (a : X.left.functionFieldˣ)
    (ω : CurveRationalDifferentials X) (hω : ω ≠ 0) :
    CurveDivisor.degree
        (differentialDivisor X ((a : X.left.functionField) • ω)
          (smul_ne_zero (Units.ne_zero a) hω)) =
      CurveDivisor.degree (differentialDivisor X ω hω) := by
  exact degree_differentialDivisor_smul_eq X a ω hω
    (smul_ne_zero (Units.ne_zero a) hω)

end
end Hartshorne
